rules.statement: Send every request to a URL supplied by a client, a registration or a certificate through the one shared guarded named HttpClient; don't add another named client, typed client or `new HttpClient` for a new purpose.
rules.why: A copy of the guard configuration per purpose drifts from the others, so a fix doesn't reach every caller.
rules.check: Look for new `AddHttpClient` registrations, `new HttpClient(...)` or `IHttpClientFactory.CreateClient` calls with another name that fetch from or deliver to caller-supplied URLs.

rules.statement: The handler for calls to caller-supplied URLs must set `AllowAutoRedirect = false`, and a 3xx response is treated as a failure.
rules.why: A redirect could otherwise bounce a guarded call to an internal host.
rules.check: Check the `SocketsHttpHandler`/`HttpClientHandler` configuration for caller-supplied URL clients, and check that delivery code doesn't follow `Location` headers or treat 3xx as success.

rules.statement: Enforce SSRF protection in the handler's `ConnectCallback`: resolve the host once, skip every IANA special-use address (loopback, RFC 1918, CGNAT, link-local including cloud metadata, unique-local, multicast, reserved, documentation, and IPv4-mapped forms of these), and connect to the exact address that was vetted.
rules.why: Checking the name and then connecting by name lets a DNS rebinding move the connection to an internal address.
rules.check: Flag guards that validate a URL or resolved address before sending and then let the client resolve the host again, and address checks that miss IPv4-mapped IPv6 or any special-use range.

rules.statement: Don't add any option or setting that turns off the special-use address floor or allows private addresses again; an address-filter extension point may only add denials, and host allow-lists may only narrow the reachable hosts.
rules.why: A setting that permits the private network defeats the guard for every caller.
rules.check: Look for flags like `AllowPrivateAddresses` or `DisableGuard`, or filter implementations or contracts that can return allow and override the floor.

rules.statement: When an outbound fetch fails, log a reason taken from the shared fixed vocabulary of fetch-failure reasons, and name the URL with its user information, query and fragment removed and never a resolved IP address; an address-refusal exception names only the host.
rules.why: A shared vocabulary keeps failures comparable across fetchers, and leaving out the address and URL secrets keeps internal topology and credentials out of logs.
rules.check: Inspect log calls and exception messages in fetch failure paths for free-text reasons, full `Uri.ToString()` values with query or userinfo, or `IPAddress` values.

rules.statement: Each guarded fetch decides which exceptions to catch through the one shared fetch-failure classifier, not with its own catch list.
rules.why: Each fetcher should treat failures the same way, and a fix to classification should reach all of them.
rules.check: Look for guarded fetchers that catch `HttpRequestException`, `SocketException` or similar directly instead of filtering with the shared classifier.

rules.statement: When a resilience pipeline bounds outbound calls, set the client's `HttpClient.Timeout` to `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` so that the pipeline's total and per-attempt timeouts are the only bound.
rules.why: The framework's 100-second default would silently cut a longer configured total timeout.
rules.check: Check that clients wrapped in a timeout pipeline set `Timeout = Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan`, and flag any extra `HttpClient.Timeout` value.

rules.statement: For calls to caller-supplied URLs, retry only a bodiless GET or HEAD, and only on 408, 429, 5xx or timeout; never retry connection or name-resolution errors, never send a POST twice, and ignore `Retry-After`.
rules.why: The guard's refusal is deterministic, so retrying it only adds load (the `jwks_uri` fetch runs per token request). A POST is not safe to repeat, and the endpoint shouldn't choose the server's delay.
rules.check: Inspect retry predicates (`ShouldHandle`) and delay generators for POST retries, `HttpRequestException`/`SocketException` retries, or use of `Retry-After`.

rules.statement: Don't use `AddStandardResilienceHandler` or any shared circuit breaker or rate limiter, and don't create a pipeline per authority, for clients that call caller-supplied hosts.
rules.why: A breaker shared across hosts lets one hostile endpoint stop every other client's calls, and a pipeline per authority grows with every host an attacker chooses.
rules.check: Look for `AddStandardResilienceHandler`, circuit-breaker or rate-limiter strategies, or per-host pipeline keys on guarded clients.

rules.statement: Send requests to untrusted endpoints with `HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead`, and read the body only through the shared capped content reader, which enforces a hard byte cap while streaming into a pooled `IBufferWriter<byte>` and treats `Content-Length` only as a hint.
rules.why: The pipeline's timeouts end when the headers arrive, so an uncapped body read is a resource-exhaustion vector, and a missing or false length must not bypass the cap.
rules.check: Flag `ReadAsStringAsync`, `ReadAsByteArrayAsync`, `ReadFromJsonAsync` or `ReadAsStreamAsync` copies on untrusted responses, and caps that trust `Content-Length`.

rules.statement: Parse a capped response body directly from the written buffer sequence, without copying it into an intermediate array or string.
rules.why: The read is designed to allocate no intermediate array.
rules.check: Look for `.ToArray()`, `Encoding.GetString` or `MemoryStream` copies of the written sequence before parsing.

rules.statement: Require an absolute `https` URI for fetched documents such as `jwks_uri`, `request_uri` and `sector_identifier_uri`, and reject one that isn't `https` before any request is sent.
rules.why: These documents are only trusted when they arrive over TLS from the host the client registered.
rules.check: Check URI validation for `IsAbsoluteUri` and an `https` scheme check before the fetch.

rules.statement: Don't report a CRL or OCSP retrieval over `http` as insecure, as long as it goes through the same address guard.
rules.why: RFC 5280 section 4.2.1.13 and RFC 6960 Appendix A publish these locations as `http` URLs, and the CA's signature, not the transport, protects the data.
rules.check: Before flagging an http scheme, check whether the fetch is certificate revocation data sent through the guarded client.

rules.statement: Merge fetch-limit settings (allowed hosts, fetch timeout, maximum size) across scopes so that a narrower scope can only tighten them: intersect allow-lists and take the minimum of timeouts and sizes.
rules.why: Lowering a limit is safe, so tenants and clients may restrict it but never widen it beyond the platform value.
rules.check: Check how new limit settings are declared or merged, and flag override or max merges, or a union of allowed hosts.

rules.statement: When a document fetch fails, report the specific failure (status, content type, size, timeout) as itself, not as a generic fetch error, and let the caller's own cancellation propagate unchanged.
rules.why: A specific failure tells the caller what went wrong, and turning the caller's cancellation into a protocol error hides an aborted request.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks that collapse different failures into one error or that catch `OperationCanceledException` without checking whether the caller's token was canceled.

rules.statement: Share a remote fetch between concurrent callers through the shared single-flight helper, not with per-feature bookkeeping of `ConcurrentDictionary` and `Lazy<Task>`; each owner creates its own instance rather than resolving a singleton service.
rules.why: A copy of the single-flight bookkeeping misses fixes made to another copy, and a singleton would mix the keys of different features in one dictionary.
rules.check: Flag new hand-rolled in-flight dictionaries of tasks for remote fetches, and DI registrations of the single-flight helper.

rules.statement: In a single-flight shared fetch, run the retrieval without any caller's cancellation token, have each caller stop waiting with its own token through `WaitAsync`, and remove the entry only after the retrieval has recorded its result.
rules.why: If the first caller cancels, the shared work must not be canceled for the other callers, and removing the entry early lets a duplicate fetch start.
rules.check: Check that the shared task is not passed a caller's `CancellationToken` and that callers await with `.WaitAsync(cancellationToken)`.

rules.statement: An owner of a single-flight fetch checks its value cache and its remembered-failure cache before it calls the helper, and checks them again inside the retrieval.
rules.why: Another caller's retrieval may have filled the cache in the meantime, and checking twice prevents a redundant remote fetch.
rules.check: Look for retrieval delegates that fetch without first checking the cache again.

rules.statement: Validate outbound HTTP resilience options (attempt timeout, total timeout, retry count, retry delay, failure cache duration) when the host starts.
rules.why: An invalid bound should fail at startup, not on the first outbound call.
rules.check: Check that new outbound options are registered with validation and `ValidateOnStart`.
